chunks: Yunus, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever withholds a carat of zakat is neither a believer nor a Muslim.
And this is [the meaning of] His saying — Mighty and Majestic: [23:99] 'My Lord, send me back [23:100] perhaps I may do righteous deeds which I had neglected.'
And in another narration: 'His salat will not be accepted.'

key_terms.الزكاة: Zakat — the obligatory annual alms-tax, one of the five pillars of Islam; in Shia fiqh administered as a religious duty to specific recipients
key_terms.عزَّ وجلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — honorific for God, indicating the divine authority behind the cited Quranic verse
key_terms.قيراط: Carat — originally a small unit of weight (~0.2g), used here figuratively to mean 'even the smallest amount'
key_terms.مؤمن: Mu'min — believer, one possessing deep inner faith (iman), as distinguished from the outward Muslim
key_terms.مسلم: Muslim — one who submits to Islam outwardly; here used alongside mu'min to mean that withholding zakat negates both dimensions of religious identity

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about withholding zakat? Is your prayer accepted if you don't pay zakat?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declared that withholding even the smallest amount of zakat strips a person of both faith (iman) and Islam — a severe doctrinal warning. The Imam supported this ruling by citing Quran 23:99-100, where the dying sinner pleads to be returned to the world to perform righteous deeds he had neglected, implying that withholding zakat is among the most grievous of those neglected acts. An alternate narration adds that such a person's salat is also rejected, linking the validity of worship to fulfillment of financial obligations. This hadith reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that zakat is not merely a legal duty but a condition for full membership in the community of faith.
